Name: Electric Motor Temperature
Summary: 185 hours of 2 Hz test bench recordings from a permanent magnet synchronous motor, for estimating rotor and stator temperatures and torque.
Description:
Electric Motor Temperature holds sensor data from a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) mounted on a test bench; the motor represents a German OEM's prototype model. The LEA department at Paderborn University recorded the measurements, and the data are shared on Kaggle under CC BY-SA 4.0.

All signals are sampled at 2 Hz in one CSV file. Measurement sessions last between one and six hours and are told apart by a profile_id column. Hand-designed driving cycles set a reference speed and torque, most of them random walks in the speed-torque plane that imitate real driving; d/q currents and voltages follow from a standard control strategy. A later update added 17 profiles, raising the total from 138 to 185 hours.

The owner names rotor temperature, stator temperatures and torque as the most interesting targets; rotor temperature and torque in particular are not reliably and economically measurable in a commercial vehicle. A related paper on deep residual learning comes with code on GitHub.
